Job Description


What you will do:
As a Software Engineer, you will be responsible for designing, developing, testing, and maintaining software applications that meet business and technical requirements. As a core member of the delivery team, the Software Engineer translates user stories into working code, contributes to system architecture and integration, and ensures code quality through best practices. The role requires strong collaboration with other engineers, architects, testers, and business analysts to deliver robust and scalable solutions.
1. Software Development & Maintenance
Develop, test, and maintain scalable and maintainable code according to technical specifications.
Troubleshoot and resolve bugs, performance issues, and system outages.
Write and maintain technical documentation.
2. System & Technical Design
Participate in system design discussions and provide input on technical decisions.
3. Cross-Functional Collaboration
Collaborate with business analysts, architects, and QA engineers to deliver user stories.
4. Code Quality, Standards & Security
Perform code reviews and ensure adherence to coding standards and security guidelines.
5. DevOps & CI/CD Enablement
Contribute to the development and improvement of CI/CD pipelines and deployment processes.
6. Continuous Learning
Stay current with emerging tools, frameworks, and development practices.


Qualifications


The ideal candidate should possess: 
2 - 5 years of relevant experience, primarily in React JS (must have) + Python (preferred)
Proficient in one or more programming languages (e.g., Java, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, C#)
Experience with web frameworks (e.g., React, Angular, Node.js, .NET, Spring Boot)
Familiarity with RESTful APIs, microservices architecture, and backend development - Experience with version control (e.g., Git), CI/CD pipelines, and DevOps practices
Exposure to containerization and orchestration (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes)
Understanding of database technologies (e.g., SQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB)
Knowledge of secure coding practices, performance optimization, and software testing (unit, integration, E2E)
Familiarity with Agile methodologies (Scrum, Kanban)


Additional Information


Why Join NCS 
Lead high-impact Data & AI advisory programs for major enterprises and public sector clients.  
Shape enterprise strategies and governance frameworks that drive real transformation.  
Work with a talented, multidisciplinary team in a collaborative environment.  
Competitive compensation and strong professional development support.  
We are driven by our AEIOU beliefs—Adventure, Excellence, Integrity, Ownership, and Unity—and we seek individuals who embody these values in both their professional and personal lives. We are committed to our Impact: Valuing our clients, Growing our people, and Creating our future.

Learn more about us at ncs.co and visit our LinkedIn career site.

We are aware of fraudulent job offers and impersonations of NCS recruiters. Phishing emails using convincing-looking but fake addresses are also commonly used to trick you into thinking that they come from official NCS sources.

title: Software Engineer (Contract)
description:
About the Role
We're looking for a problem-solver first, developer second.
In this role, you won't just be writing code from a spec. You'll be thinking through features, anticipating edge cases, and building systems that actually work in production. When we say "build a voucher system," we expect you to ask: What's the max per customer? Is there a global cap? What happens when it expires mid-checkout? Can it stack with other discounts?
You'll work on real-world logistics, retail, and operational challenges powering a fast-scaling laundry-tech platform. Our tech stack includes:
Backend: Laravel PHP, Node.js/Express with TypeScript & Prisma (microservices architecture)
Frontend: Next.js 15 with React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
Databases: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis
IoT Services: Python (FastAPI/Flask) for machine integrations via Modbus protocol
Infrastructure: Docker, queue workers (Beanstalkd), Firebase, AWS S3
This role is NOT for you if:
• You wait to be told exactly what to build
• You struggle to debug issues independently
• You've never thought about edge cases before they became bugs in production
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

• Design and implement features end-to-end – from understanding the business problem to thinking through edge cases to writing clean, maintainable code
• Debug and troubleshoot – we need someone who can trace through logs, reproduce issues, and fix root causes (not just symptoms)
• Think before you code – document your approach, consider failure modes, and propose solutions before jumping into implementation
• Collaborate across teams – work with frontend/mobile engineers, ops, and business stakeholders to ship features that actually solve problems
Requirements
• 2–5 years of hands-on PHP/JS stack development
• Strong problem-solving skills – you can break down ambiguous requirements into concrete implementation steps
• MySQL query optimization and indexing at scale
• Experience with RESTful APIs and Microservice architecture
• Comfortable debugging in production – you know how to trace issues through logs, queues, and database queries
• Git flow version control and structured deployment experience
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Nice to Have

• Microservices architecture and service-to-service communication
• Familiarity with Redis, queue workers, and job scheduling
• IoT device integration or hardware protocols (Modbus, serial communication)
• Docker, containerization, and cloud deployment (AWS, DigitalOcean)
• Linux CLI, bash scripting, and DevOps practices
• Can communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical teams
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
How We Evaluate
We don't just test coding ability. Our interview process includes:
Technical Discussion – Walk us through a feature you've built. Show us your code, explain your decisions, demonstrate how it works.
Problem-Solving Exercise – Given a business requirement, show us how you'd think through the design, edge cases, and implementation approach.

We're looking for engineers who think ahead, not just developers who write code.

title: Software Engineer & Coding Instructor
description:
About the job
We desperately need someone who does real software engineering, not just ‘theory’ teaching
We are building the future of tech education.
A learning portal powered by 
AI
, with 
real courses
, not just slides or videos. We need someone who writes production-grade code 
and
 can teach it. If “you actually build stuff” is your baseline, read on.
What pains we are feeling now
These are the problems keeping us up at night:
Our learning platform is brittle. Adding new courses, new assignments, new content types feels like wrestling spaghetti.
Students complain we don’t ship features fast enough — especially around interactive labs, feedback loops, auto-grading, or adaptive content.
We have brilliant AI tools we want to integrate (e.g. auto-feedback on code, adaptive difficulty) but no one to architect and build the core plumbing to support them.
Our instructors are good, but many have never been full-stack software engineers. We need curriculum creators who know the trade, the frameworks, the pitfalls.
We want to lead, not follow. That means staying ahead of what students will need: current DevOps practices, cloud infrastructure, modern frontend/backends, AI tools.
What this role will actually solve
If you join us as Lead Software Engineer & Coding Instructor, you will:
Design, build, and maintain 
the core infrastructure
 for the learning portal: course delivery, lab environments, auto-grading, student dashboards, version control, real-time collaboration etc.
Lead a small team of instructors / software engineers: mentor them, set coding standards, perform code reviews.
Build new courses end-to-end: architecture, content, labs, assessments, AI integration.
Work closely with AI/ML folks to integrate intelligence: e.g. auto-feedback systems, adaptive content paths, error prediction, possibly code completion.
Shape how we teach: you will not just code, but teach. You’ll design and deliver lessons, workshops, projects — ones you yourself would have liked when learning.
Make technical decisions: stack, frameworks, deployment, auto-scaling, monitoring, CI/CD.
What we need you to bring
We don’t want someone who just “could teach.” We want someone who 
currently builds
 and has done it.
Must haves:
2+ years of software engineering in production environments: backend + frontend + infrastructure.
Deep experience in at least one modern full-stack web framework (e.g. Node.js, Django, Ruby on Rails, Go, etc.), and in modern frontend frameworks (React, Vue, Svelte, etc.).
Strong understanding of deployment, scaling, monitoring, CI/CD pipelines.
Excellent code quality habits, test coverage, version control discipline.
Excellent communication: can explain complicated concepts simply, can write docs, mentor juniors.
You must believe “learning by doing”, “real code”, “projects not slides” is how students grow.
Nice-to-haves:
Experience with AI/ML tooling (feedback, auto grade, adaptive systems)
Experience in education technology / learning management systems or platforms
Prior teaching / mentoring experience
Familiarity with cloud services (AWS/GCP/Azure) and serverless or containerization
Open source contributions or published technical content/projects
Experience integrating AI feedback or code evaluation systems
What you’ll own & rewards
Autonomy
: this is a lead role. You will make decisions and define tech roadmap in collaboration with the leadership.
Impact
: what you build will be used by hundreds or thousands of students. The quality, architecture, UX are not just academic — they matter deeply.
Growth
: opportunity to lead, teach, grow the engineering side, curriculum design, possibly build your own team under you.
Learning
: you’ll be working with AI/ML folks, educational designers, and other engineers — you’ll stretch beyond “just coding.”
Compensation
: competitive market rate + equity, benefits, and flexibility.
Who this is not for
You’re probably not right for this if:
• You’ve never shipped production apps, just toy projects or coursework.
• You dislike teaching, explaining, mentoring.
• You prefer solo work only, and hate dealing with content, pedagogy, student feedback.
• You want a role that’s “just lecture slides” or “just coding behind the scenes” — we need someone bridging both worlds.
If you read this and thought “YES, that sounds like me"
Apply here: sig1.co/apply-job
Send us a note with:
What large-scale code projects you’ve architected, built, maintained (include tech stack).
One example where you taught someone or built educational content: project, workshops, or mentoring.
Something you built 
just for yourself
 (side project / open source) that shows you solve hard problems.
What you think is the biggest technical/UX challenge in “learning portals with AI” today.

title: Software Engineer & Tech Instructors
description:
About the job
We need someone who does real software engineering, not just ‘theory’ teaching
We are building the future of tech education.
A learning portal powered by AI, with real courses, not just slides or videos. We need someone who writes production-grade code 
and
 can teach it. If “you actually build stuff” is your baseline, read on.
What pains we are feeling now
These are the problems keeping us up at night:
Our learning platform is brittle. Adding new courses, new assignments, new content types feels like wrestling spaghetti.
Students complain we don’t ship features fast enough — especially around interactive labs, feedback loops, auto-grading, or adaptive content.
We have brilliant AI tools we want to integrate (e.g. auto-feedback on code, adaptive difficulty) but no one to architect and build the core plumbing to support them.
Our instructors are good, but many have never been full-stack software engineers. We need curriculum creators who know the trade, the frameworks, the pitfalls.
We want to lead, not follow. That means staying ahead of what students will need: current DevOps practices, cloud infrastructure, modern frontend/backends, AI tools.
What this role will actually solve
If you join us as Software Engineer & Coding Instructor, you will:
Design, build, and maintain the core infrastructure for the learning portal: course delivery, lab environments, auto-grading, student dashboards, version control, real-time collaboration etc.
Lead a small team of instructors / software engineers: mentor them, set coding standards, perform code reviews.
Build new courses end-to-end: architecture, content, labs, assessments, AI integration.
Work closely with AI/ML folks to integrate intelligence: e.g. auto-feedback systems, adaptive content paths, error prediction, possibly code completion.
Shape how we teach: you will not just code, but teach. You’ll design and deliver lessons, workshops, projects — ones you yourself would have liked when learning.
Make technical decisions: stack, frameworks, deployment, auto-scaling, monitoring, CI/CD.
Must haves:
2+ year of software engineering in production environments: backend + frontend + infrastructure.
Deep experience in at least one modern full-stack web framework (e.g. Node.js, Django, Ruby on Rails, Go, etc.), and in modern frontend frameworks (React, Vue, Svelte, etc.).
Strong understanding of deployment, scaling, monitoring, CI/CD pipelines.
Excellent code quality habits, test coverage, version control discipline.
Excellent communication: can explain complicated concepts simply, can write docs, mentor juniors.
You must believe “learning by doing”, “real code”, “projects not slides” is how students grow.
Nice-to-haves:
Experience with AI/ML tooling (feedback, auto grade, adaptive systems)
Experience in education technology / learning management systems or platforms
Prior teaching / mentoring experience
Familiarity with cloud services (AWS/GCP/Azure) and serverless or containerization
Open source contributions or published technical content/projects
Experience integrating AI feedback or code evaluation systems
What you’ll own & rewards
Autonomy: this is a lead role. You will make decisions and define tech roadmap in collaboration with the leadership.
Impact: what you build will be used by hundreds or thousands of students. The quality, architecture, UX are not just academic — they matter deeply.
Growth: opportunity to lead, teach, grow the engineering side, curriculum design, possibly build your own team under you.
Learning: you’ll be working with AI/ML folks, educational designers, and other engineers — you’ll stretch beyond “just coding.”
Compensation: competitive market rate + equity, benefits, and flexibility.
Who this is not for
You’re probably not right for this if:
• You’ve never shipped production apps, just toy projects or coursework.
• You dislike teaching, explaining, mentoring.
• You prefer solo work only, and hate dealing with content, pedagogy, student feedback.
• You want a role that’s “just lecture slides” or “just coding behind the scenes” — we need someone bridging both worlds.
If you read this and thought “YES, that sounds like me"
Apply here: sig1.co/apply-job
Send us a note with:
What large-scale code projects you’ve architected, built, maintained (include tech stack).
One example where you taught someone or built educational content: project, workshops, or mentoring.
Something you built 
just for yourself
 (side project / open source) that shows you solve hard problems.
What you think is the biggest technical/UX challenge in “learning portals with AI” today.

title: Software Engineering & Tech Instructor
description:
About the job
We desperately need someone who does real software engineering, not just ‘theory’ teaching
We are building the future of tech education.
A learning portal powered by AI, with real courses, not just slides or videos. We need someone who writes production-grade code 
and
 can teach it. If “you actually build stuff” is your baseline, read on.
What pains we are feeling now
These are the problems keeping us up at night:
Our learning platform is brittle. Adding new courses, new assignments, new content types feels like wrestling spaghetti.
Students complain we don’t ship features fast enough — especially around interactive labs, feedback loops, auto-grading, or adaptive content.
We have brilliant AI tools we want to integrate (e.g. auto-feedback on code, adaptive difficulty) but no one to architect and build the core plumbing to support them.
Our instructors are good, but many have never been full-stack software engineers. We need curriculum creators who know the trade, the frameworks, the pitfalls.
We want to lead, not follow. That means staying ahead of what students will need: current DevOps practices, cloud infrastructure, modern frontend/backends, AI tools.
What this role will actually solve
If you join us as Lead Software Engineer & Coding Instructor, you will:
Design, build, and maintain the core infrastructure for the learning portal: course delivery, lab environments, auto-grading, student dashboards, version control, real-time collaboration etc.
Lead a small team of instructors / software engineers: mentor them, set coding standards, perform code reviews.
Build new courses end-to-end: architecture, content, labs, assessments, AI integration.
Work closely with AI/ML folks to integrate intelligence: e.g. auto-feedback systems, adaptive content paths, error prediction, possibly code completion.
Shape how we teach: you will not just code, but teach. You’ll design and deliver lessons, workshops, projects — ones you yourself would have liked when learning.
Make technical decisions: stack, frameworks, deployment, auto-scaling, monitoring, CI/CD.
Must haves:
2+ year of software engineering in production environments: backend + frontend + infrastructure.
Deep experience in at least one modern full-stack web framework (e.g. Node.js, Django, Ruby on Rails, Go, etc.), and in modern frontend frameworks (React, Vue, Svelte, etc.).
Strong understanding of deployment, scaling, monitoring, CI/CD pipelines.
Excellent code quality habits, test coverage, version control discipline.
Excellent communication: can explain complicated concepts simply, can write docs, mentor juniors.
You must believe “learning by doing”, “real code”, “projects not slides” is how students grow.
Nice-to-haves:
Experience with AI/ML tooling (feedback, auto grade, adaptive systems)
Experience in education technology / learning management systems or platforms
Prior teaching / mentoring experience
Familiarity with cloud services (AWS/GCP/Azure) and serverless or containerization
Open source contributions or published technical content/projects
Experience integrating AI feedback or code evaluation systems
What you’ll own & rewards
Autonomy: this is a lead role. You will make decisions and define tech roadmap in collaboration with the leadership.
Impact: what you build will be used by hundreds or thousands of students. The quality, architecture, UX are not just academic — they matter deeply.
Growth: opportunity to lead, teach, grow the engineering side, curriculum design, possibly build your own team under you.
Learning: you’ll be working with AI/ML folks, educational designers, and other engineers — you’ll stretch beyond “just coding.”
Compensation: competitive market rate + equity, benefits, and flexibility.
Who this is not for
You’re probably not right for this if:
• You’ve never shipped production apps, just toy projects or coursework.
• You dislike teaching, explaining, mentoring.
• You prefer solo work only, and hate dealing with content, pedagogy, student feedback.
• You want a role that’s “just lecture slides” or “just coding behind the scenes” — we need someone bridging both worlds.
If you read this and thought “YES, that sounds like me"
Apply here: sig1.co/apply-job
Send us a note with:
What large-scale code projects you’ve architected, built, maintained (include tech stack).
One example where you taught someone or built educational content: project, workshops, or mentoring.
Something you built 
just for yourself
 (side project / open source) that shows you solve hard problems.
What you think is the biggest technical/UX challenge in “learning portals with AI” today.

 engineering role.

proposals
architecture notes
async updates
documentation

learn
break through
switch careers
become software engineers

AI, devtools, Jamstack trends, DX improvements, you stay updated.

You want rigid instructions instead of autonomy

You hate writing or documenting decisions
You dislike education or mentoring others
You want a purely engineering role with no product thinking

title: Product & UI/UX Designer
description:
About the job
Why This Role Exists
Sigma School is building the next-generation learning portal for Southeast Asia: a platform where people learn to code, stay motivated, build community, and get hired. The current online learning experience in the region is dull, transactional, and isolating. Students quit because traditional LMS platforms are boring, confusing, or lack credibility with employers.
We want a product designer who can rethink this from the ground up.
You will create an experience that is clean, addictive to use, socially engaging, and trusted by employers. Your work shapes how thousands of students learn, stay accountable, and showcase their skills.
What You Will Build
You will design the full learning journey: lessons, quizzes, projects, assessments, student dashboards, and public profiles. You will also design engagement systems like streaks, badges, XP, micro-interactions, confetti, challenges, and community features that make learning feel fun and rewarding.
Your job is to make the product something students naturally return to every day.
What You Will Do
•⁠ ⁠Own the end-to-end UX for the learning portal from wireframes to high-fidelity UI
•⁠ ⁠Design clean interfaces that feel lightweight, compact, and information-rich
•⁠ ⁠Turn complex learning workflows into intuitive experiences
•⁠ ⁠Create gamification elements such as streaks, badges, XP, progress trackers, and delightful UI moments
•⁠ ⁠Design social features including learner profiles, leaderboards, comments, challenges, and sharing loops
•⁠ ⁠Design real assessment flows similar to HackerRank: submissions, scoring, feedback, difficulty states
•⁠ ⁠Collaborate deeply with product, engineering, content teams
•⁠ ⁠Run usability tests and iterate based on student behavior and data
•⁠ ⁠Maintain a consistent design system aligned with our branding and component library
•⁠ ⁠Ship fast, improve fast, and think like an owner
What Success Looks Like
•⁠ ⁠Higher lesson completion and course graduation rates
•⁠ ⁠Students return more frequently (higher DAU, better retention)
•⁠ ⁠Students enjoy learning because the product feels rewarding
•⁠ ⁠Social and community features increase sharing and referrals
•⁠ ⁠Employers trust our assessments and use them to hire talent
•⁠ ⁠The learning portal looks and feels like a modern, world-class product
What You Should Bring
•⁠ ⁠2+ years in product/UI/UX design with real shipped products
•⁠ ⁠A portfolio showing strong interaction design, not just landing pages
•⁠ ⁠Ability to simplify complex workflows
•⁠ ⁠Understanding of behavior design, motivation, habit loops, or gamification
•⁠ ⁠Experience designing social/community features is a plus
•⁠ ⁠Experience with edtech or assessment products is a strong advantage
•⁠ ⁠Strong Figma skills
•⁠ ⁠Clear communication and ability to collaborate with engineers
•⁠ ⁠High ownership, fast execution, and willingness to iterate
Who Thrives Here
People who think in systems, not just screens. People who take pride in shipping work that users love. People who enjoy education, learning, and building tools that change real lives. People who can balance aesthetics, speed, and usability without needing micromanagement.

title: IT エンジニア - 日本人募集
description:
世界的に影響力のあるソフトウェア企業のプロジェクトになります。
【職務の概要】
会社で使用するWindowsデバイス（PCなど）の管理、セットアップ、導入をスムーズに行う、主体性と正確さを備えた担当者を募集しています。
この役割の主なミッションは、パソコンの導入準備から、日々の設定、そして廃棄（リプレイス）まで、デバイスの「一生（ライフサイクル）」を管理し、ユーザーがストレスなく仕事ができる環境を整えることです。
【主な業務内容】
・パソコンの管理：社内で使うノートPCやデスクトップ、周辺機器の導入から廃棄までをまるごと管理します。
・初期設定（キッティング）：自動化ツールや決められた手順（標準イメージ）を使って、パソコンを使える状態にセットアップします。
・管理ツールの運用：Microsoft Intuneなどの管理ツールを使い、遠隔でパソコンの設定や登録を行います。
・利用準備：新しいユーザーのために、中身のシステム（OS）を整え、必要な設定を済ませます。
・入れ替えサポート：パソコンの買い替えや交換、古い端末の回収・廃棄をサポートします。
・トラブル解決：パソコン本体、OS、初期設定に関連するトラブルの原因を突き止め、解決します。
・ルールの徹底：すべてのパソコンが、会社のセキュリティルール通りに設定されているか確認します。
・更新プログラムの管理：最新のOSアップデートや、周辺機器を動かすソフト（ドライバー）を常に最新の状態に保ちます。
・周辺機器のサポート：モニターやドッキングステーション、USB接続機器などの困りごとを助けます。
・マニュアル作成：設定の手順や、トラブルが起きた時の解決方法を文書にまとめます。
・ユーザーへの説明：入社時や新しいパソコンを渡す際、使い方の説明や設定のアドバイスを行います。
職種：IT エンジニア
勤務時間：月〜金、9:00〜18:00（祝日出勤あり、その場合は振替休日を付与）
注意：将来的に勤務時間が変更する可能性があります
KPI ：支給あり
言語要件：日本語が流暢であること ＋ 英語初級および中級程度（A2レベル）
必要な資格と経験
【経験】
テクニカルサポート、コンサルティング、またはIT分野での実務経験が最低2年以上あること。
または、コンピューターサイエンス（CS）もしくはIT系の学士号を保有し、かつWindowsシステム管理の実務経験が2年以上あること。
【技術的な熟練度】（以下の項目に精通していること）
・Windowsの基本構造: レジストリ、ファイルシステム、ユーザーアカウント、およびACL（アクセス制御リスト）
・ログと監視: イベントログ、監査、パフォーマンスモニタリング（PerfMon、リソースモニター）
・ネットワーク: TCP/IP、DNS、SMB、Kerberos、PKI（公開鍵暗号基盤）
・仮想化・サーバー管理: Hyper-V、SDN（ソフトウェア定義ネットワーク）、クラスタリング、レジリエント・ストレージ
・管理ツール: PowerShell、Group Policy、BitLocker、Windows Update、およびShell構成

ABOUT THE ENERGY COMMISSION:
A statutory body established under the Energy Commission Act 2001, Suruhanjaya Tenaga (ST) or the Energy Commission is responsible for regulating the energy sector, specifically the electricity and piped gas supply industries, in Peninsular Malaysia.
Taking over the role of the Department of Electricity and Gas Supply, the Energy Commission started its operation on January 1, 2002. The main focus of the commission is reliable electricity and gas supply, reasonable costs and safety.
The roles of the Energy Commission are divided into three, namely Economic Regulation, Technical Regulation and Safety Regulation.
Economic Regulation:
To promote economy in the generation, transmission, distribution, supply and use of electricity and in the reticulation and use of gas; promote competition; enable fair and efficient market conduct and prevent the misuse of monopoly or market power in the electricity and piped gas industries.
Technical Regulation:
To ensure security, reliability, efficiency and quality of supply and services in the electricity and piped gas supply industries.
Safety Regulation:
To protect the industry, consumers and public from dangers arising from the generation, transmission, distribution, supply and use of electricity and the distribution, supply and use of piped gas.

title: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Engineer – Microsoft Purview

Position Description:


We are seeking a Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Engineer with 2+ years of experience to support the build, configuration, testing, and rollout of a Microsoft Purview DLP program for a large enterprise environment. The scope focuses on enabling unified detection, protection, and control of sensitive data across endpoints and Microsoft 365 workloads, including Office 365, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Microsoft Teams, as well as optimizing and re-enabling email DLP.


Working under the technical direction of the DLP Architect, you will implement policies and configurations, execute pilots and wave-based deployment, monitor alerts and detection quality, and support tuning and aftercare activities. You’ll collaborate closely with the Project Manager, Compliance Analyst, Data Governance Lead, and Trainer to ensure the solution is effective, scalable, and user-ready.






Your future duties and responsibilities:


1) Purview DLP Build & Configuration
• Configure Microsoft Purview DLP policies and rules based on provided design (scoping, conditions, actions, user notifications, overrides/justifications, and enforcement modes).
• Implement policy components correctly and consistently across workloads, following agreed standards and governance.
• Support configuration of classification elements leveraged by DLP (e.g., Sensitive Information Types, sensitivity labels, and workload-specific policy settings).


2) Microsoft 365 Workload Enablement
• Implement and validate DLP coverage across Microsoft 365 workloads, including:
 -Exchange Online / Email DLP (re-enable and optimize baseline rules)
 -SharePoint Online & OneDrive for Business (including external sharing controls where required)
 -Microsoft Teams (policy alignment for chats/messages where applicable; files governed via SharePoint/OneDrive)
• Configure user experience controls such as policy tips/notifications and align them to change/adoption requirements.


3) Endpoint DLP Onboarding & Controls
• Support endpoint onboarding and readiness activities (prerequisites, deployment coordination, validation), aligned to the client’s tooling (e.g., Intune and Defender for Endpoint).
• Configure and test endpoint DLP scenarios (e.g., copying to removable media, printing, uploads to browser/web destinations, and other risky actions), aligned to “monitor → tune → enforce” rollout discipline.


4) Pilot Execution & Wave-Based Rollout
• Execute pilot configurations and validate detections and user prompts with pilot users/business units.
• Support controlled enterprise rollout in waves (e.g., by business unit), including deployment checklists, validation steps, rollback/mitigation plans, and hypercare readiness.


5) Monitoring, Troubleshooting & Policy Tuning Support
• Monitor DLP alerts, event telemetry, and reporting to assess signal quality and operational impact.
• Investigate false positives/false negatives and propose tuning adjustments (rule thresholds, conditions, exclusions, scoping changes) for approval by the DLP Architect and stakeholders.
• Support operational workflows for triage and escalation (service desk and security/compliance stakeholders).


6) Integration & Automation Support
• Assist with integrating DLP alerting into broader security operations workflows (e.g., Microsoft Defender XDR and/or Microsoft Sentinel if used).
• Support automation tasks where required (e.g., reporting workflows, alert routing, operational dashboards), leveraging PowerShell and/or Power Automate as appropriate.


7) Documentation, Handover & Enablement
• Produce and maintain implementation documentation: configuration records, test evidence, operational runbooks, and support guides.
• Support the Trainer and project team with enablement materials, including service desk readiness and end-user guidance (microlearning/policy awareness content).






Required qualifications to be successful in this role:


• 2+ years of experience in DLP, information protection, Microsoft 365 security/compliance, or security engineering.
• Hands-on experience configuring or supporting Microsoft Purview DLP (or closely related Microsoft 365 compliance/security controls) across one or more workloads (Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams) and/or endpoints.
• Working understanding of the DLP lifecycle (plan/design, implement, test, monitor, tune, enforce/hypercare).
• Familiarity with key enabling tools and concepts such as:
 -Microsoft Purview compliance portal
 -Sensitive Information Types (SITs), sensitivity labels, and policy scoping
 -PowerShell for administration and reporting support
 -Endpoint management/security concepts (e.g., Intune / Microsoft Defender for Endpoint)
• Strong troubleshooting mindset, attention to detail, and ability to follow change control and deployment governance.
• Good communication skills and comfort working in a client-facing, structured delivery environment.


Strong Advantage (Preferred)
• Experience with endpoint DLP at scale (large device populations and wave deployments).
• Experience with DLP policy tips, user prompts, and adoption-focused configurations for SharePoint/OneDrive.
• Exposure to Microsoft security/compliance certifications (e.g., SC-400) or equivalent hands-on capability.
• Experience integrating DLP alerts with SOC workflows and tooling (Microsoft Defender XDR, Sentinel) and/or building operational dashboards (Power BI).
• Experience in regulated environments and alignment with data protection expectations (e.g., GDPR-type obligations).


Success Profile at CGI

• Collaborative and coachable: works effectively with the DLP Architect and cross-functional stakeholders (PM, compliance, governance, training, service desk).

 For the critical hot-paths of the execution engine.

This role is passionate about engineering reliable, scalable, and API-driven directory services. You will drive the adoption of Infrastructure as Code (IaC), Configuration as Code (CaC), and Posture Management as Code, ensuring that directory operations follow modern engineering principles.

This is a critical engineering role where you will work with IAM, security, and cloud teams to build a next-generation directory services platform.


What you will deliver




Modernizing Directory Infrastructure - Implement Infrastructure as Code (IaC), Configuration as Code (CaC), and Posture as Code to automate and improve reliability.


Building API-Driven Directory Services - Enable self-service access to key directory functions (e.g., account creation, group management, DNS) via APIs.


Ensuring Secure & Scalable Operations - Apply platform engineering standard methodologies to build a scalable, resilient, and automated directory platform.


Supporting AD to Entra ID Transition - Assist in the gradual migration from on-prem Active Directory to Entra ID, ensuring a magnificent user experience.


Improving CI/CD & GitOps Practices - Ensure all directory changes follow CI/CD pipelines, GitOps workflows, and policy enforcement.


Cross-Platform IAM Integration - Work closely with IAM, cloud, and security teams to ensure a cohesive identity ecosystem.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in technology, Engineering, or a related field.


Identity & Access Management (IAM) Expertise


Shown understanding of Active Directory (AD) & Entra ID (AAD), including domain management, directory synchronization, and identity security.


Understanding modern IAM architectures, including Zero Trust, workload identity, and federated authentication.




Platform Engineering & Automation


Experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Pulumi, CloudFormation or similar) and Configuration as Code (Ansible, Chef, Puppet etc).


Experience implementing CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Azure DevOps) and GitOps or equivalent experience workflows.


Strong programming/scripting skills (Python, PowerShell, Go, Bash) for automation and infrastructure management.


Experience with observability, monitoring, and logging tools (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK Stack, Azure Monitor or similar).




Security & Compliance


Strong understanding of identity security standard methodologies, Zero Trust models, and IAM compliance frameworks (ISO 27001, NIST, CIS Benchmarks).


Experience with Posture as Code for security configuration management and drift detection.




API & Integration Knowledge


Experience working with REST APIs, Graph API, SCIM, and integrating IAM services into cloud-native applications.


Ability to expose directory services (DNS, account creation, group management) via APIs for self-service and automation.




Essential skills
We expect all engineers in our organization to align with the following principles:




Automation-First Approach - You build automated, self-service, and infrastructure-as-code solutions to reduce manual effort.

title: IT Systems Administrator (L2 - Intermediate level)
description:
IT Systems Administrator (L2 - Intermediate level)
Location: Malaysia Schedule: Sunday to Thursday, 8:30am to 5:00pm Department: Central Services
This role exists to keep client environments stable.
You focus on preventative maintenance, patch management, and infrastructure health across all clients. You work from alerts, maintenance schedules, and health reports, not from client calls or ticket noise.
If you like routine, ownership, and finishing what you start, this role fits. If you need variety, adrenaline, or constant change, it will not.
What You Will Own
You are responsible for maintaining servers and network infrastructure across standardized client environments.
Your core responsibilities include:
File Server upgrades and patching (or other operations)
Monitoring and responding to alerts from servers and network devices
Patch management for Windows servers and supported infrastructure
Verifying systems reboot correctly after patching
Rolling back failed patches and escalating when required
Troubleshooting and resolving backup failures, especially file servers
Performing firmware updates on firewalls, switches, and access points
Maintaining and cleaning up technical documentation
Producing weekly maintenance and patch compliance reports
You act first. If you are blocked for about 30 minutes or risk increases, you escalate to the Escalation Engineer in Canada.
Technologies you must be comfortable with
You are expected to operate these technologies at the maintenance and troubleshooting level, not at the design or architecture level.
MFA platforms: Duo, Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator
Microsoft Windows Server 2012 and newer
Microsoft Entra ID, Office 365, Active Directory, Azure AD Connect
Patch management methodologies and verification practices
Virtualization platforms: VMware, Hyper-V
Networking equipment: Cisco, HP, Ubiquiti, Dell
Firewalls: Fortinet, SonicWall, Sophos, Cisco ASA, Meraki
You should understand what commonly breaks, how to verify recovery, and when to stop and escalate.
How success is measured
You are successful when:
Patch compliance improves and stays within a 7-day SLA
Backup failures are caught and resolved quickly
Servers and network devices remain stable and predictable
Maintenance work is completed consistently and on schedule
Issues are escalated early, not hidden or delayed
If nothing breaks, you did your job.
What this role is not
Not a project engineer role
Not client-facing
Not a network or security architect role
This is a focused operational role.
What we are looking for
You should have:
Strong hands-on experience with Windows Server environments
Proven networking knowledge, this is mandatory
Experience maintaining virtualized environments
Confidence working independently without constant direction
Fluent in written and spoken English
A steady, disciplined work style
You will not succeed here if you freeze when something goes wrong or wait for someone else to tell you what to do.
Growth
This is an L2 role with a future path toward L3 and project work. That progression depends on consistency, judgment, and trust built over time, not speed.

title: Network Operation Center Manager (NOC Manager for DWDM)
description:
Network Operations Center Manager Position (NOC Manager)
A NOC (Network Operations Center) Manager DWDM (Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing) environment is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day operations and performance of the DWDM optical network infrastructure. This role combines general NOC management responsibilities with specific expertise in DWDM technology.
Key Responsibilities:
Operational Oversight:
Manage and direct the NOC team to ensure 24/7 monitoring, incident detection, and resolution for the DWDM network. This includes ensuring adherence to Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Service Level Agreements (SLAs), and uptime targets.
Incident and Problem Management:
Lead critical incident response and escalation for DWDM-related issues. Manage the entire incident lifecycle, from detection to resolution, often applying ITIL principles. Drive Root Cause Analysis (RCA) for recurring problems and implement continuous service improvements.
Performance Monitoring and Optimization:
Oversee the monitoring of DWDM network performance and capacity, including optical power levels, signal-to-noise ratios, and traffic utilization. Identify and address performance bottlenecks and proactively optimize the network for efficiency and stability.
DWDM-Specific Troubleshooting:
Provide advanced technical support and guidance to the NOC team for troubleshooting complex DWDM issues, including fiber cuts, equipment failures, and optical path problems. This may involve using specialized test equipment.
Vendor Management:
Liaise with third-party vendors for DWDM equipment and services, managing backhaul network issues and escalating problems as needed to ensure timely resolution.
Team Leadership and Development:
Supervise, mentor, and train NOC engineers and technicians, ensuring they possess the necessary skills and knowledge to manage the DWDM network effectively. Conduct performance reviews and manage staffing, scheduling, and on-call rotations.
Documentation and Reporting:
Ensure comprehensive documentation of network configurations, procedures, and incident reports related to the DWDM infrastructure. Generate regular performance reports and communicate network status to stakeholders.
Change Management:
Oversee the implementation of network changes and upgrades within the DWDM environment, ensuring proper planning, execution, and documentation to minimize service disruption.
Security and Compliance:
Ensure adherence to all company policies and industry standards related to network security and data privacy within the DWDM domain.
Qualifications:
Typically requires a Bachelor's degree in a related field (e.g., Telecommunications, IT) and several years of experience in network operations, with a significant focus on DWDM or optical networks.
Strong understanding of DWDM technology, including optical components, transmission principles, and network architectures.
Experience with network monitoring tools and incident management systems.
Leadership and team management skills.
Excellent problem-solving, communication, and analytical skills.
Relevant certifications (e.g., Cisco CCNA, Huawei HCIA-Transmission) are often preferred.

Peplink helps businesses around the world to make connectivity reliable and simple by developing wired and wireless routers, software and technologies. Peplink is under Plover Bay Technologies Limited, a listed company on the main board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (1523.HK).
About This Job
The role focused on providing technical assistance and support for networks leveraging Peplink and Pepwave technologies. This role is crucial to help the customer for maintaining network stability and assisting customers with guidance on configurations, troubleshooting, and understanding Peplink's SD-WAN solutions, bonding technologies, and services. The ideal candidate will have a foundational understanding of networking principles and a strong eagerness to learn and specialize in the Peplink ecosystem. You will form part of a team that provides 24/7 technical support services all year round including public holidays at the relevant time slots.

(A) Technical Support & Troubleshooting:
1.  Provide Level 1 and Level 2 remote technical support for customer networks using Peplink products and services.

3.  Process the support tickets, identifying and escalating recurring issues to senior staff.
4.  Advise customers with basic configuration of Peplink devices, including initial setup, WAN/LAN settings, firewall rules, and firmware updates.

SpeedFusion Connect and various SpeedFusion VPN modes (e.g., Hot Failover, Bonding, WAN Smoothing). 
InControl 2 (IC2) cloud management platform for device monitoring, configuration, and remote troubleshooting.
PrimeCare features and services.
Load Balancing algorithms and concepts.

3.  Stay current with new Peplink product releases, features, and software updates.

1.  When needed, document all support activities, troubleshooting steps, and resolutions in the ticketing system for knowledge base creation.
2.  Create and maintain internal documentation, guides, and procedures for common Peplink configurations and troubleshooting steps.
3.  Participate in live troubleshooting or scheduled maintenance windows as the situation is required.

Education: Associate's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Experience: 0-2 years of experience in network support, IT helpdesk, or a related technical role.

Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a professional and patient demeanor.
Certification (Preferred but not required): Entry-level networking certification (e.g., CompTIA Network+, CCNA) or, ideally, Peplink Certified Sales Specialist (PCSS) or Peplink Certified Technical Specialist (PCTS).

Eagerness to learn and specialize in SD-WAN technology, specifically Peplink/Pepwave.
Strong problem-solving and analytical abilities.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment.

title: Quality Manager
description:
Job Responsibilities
1. Conduct in-process, finished product, and incoming purchased material inspections to ensure compliance with technical specifications and standards.
2. Monitor production operations to verify adherence to quality specifications, and compile and submit inspection findings reports accurately and timely.
3. Prepare, maintain, and manage comprehensive inspection records, including documentation of product acceptance, rejection, and rework requirements, ensuring data integrity and traceability.
4. Set up, adjust, and operate inspection equipment; perform routine checks to validate equipment accuracy and reliability for quality testing.
5. Verify that all applicable drawings, specifications, and technical documents are of the latest revision before conducting inspection or production-related activities.
6. Ensure all measuring and test equipment (M&TE) is calibrated to current standards, with valid calibration labels affixed, prior to use; oversee M&TE calibration management.
7. Perform piece part and receiving inspections, including dimensional measurement, visual inspection, non-destructive testing (NDT), and hardness testing as required by technical standards.
8. Lead, supervise, and provide professional guidance to the quality team; allocate workload, monitor performance, and drive continuous improvement in team efficiency and quality awareness.
9. Plan, lead, and conduct internal audits in accordance with ISO standards; follow up on audit findings, track corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), and ensure effective closure.
10. Interpret and communicate quality control specifications, schematics, and engineering drawings accurately to the team and cross-functional departments.
11. Maintain and update the calibration database for all inspection and test equipment; ensure data is up-to-date, complete, and accessible for audit and traceability purposes.
12. Coordinate the calibration of equipment, including arranging outsourcing services for specialized calibration and managing in-house calibration activities to meet regulatory and operational requirements.
13. Oversee supplier quality management: conduct incoming inspection of supplier-provided products, track and evaluate supplier performance, and maintain detailed supplier quality records.
14. Lead and execute all inspection-related activities for components and assemblies within the WFT (Workshop/Facility Team) scope.
15. Responsible for conducting pre-loadout inspections and DROPS (Damage, Rupture, Overload, Pollution, Stability) checks on all equipment prior to shipment, ensuring compliance with delivery quality standards.
16. Compile, organize, and maintain accurate QA documentation for all corporate assets, ensuring compliance with company policies, industry regulations, and audit requirements.
17. Ensure all assigned tasks and quality activities are performed to the highest quality standards; drive a culture of quality excellence across the organization and cross-functional teams.
 
Job Requirements
Core Technical Skills
: Proficient in 8D Report preparation and analysis; familiar with ISO system procedures, and skilled in FMEA, CAPA management to support quality improvement and audit activities.
Professional Knowledge
: Extensive expertise in manufacturing process quality control, or the ability to quickly master relevant knowledge; familiarity with Six Sigma methodology, with Green Belt/Black Belt certification being a significant advantage.
Soft Skills
: Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities; excellent interpersonal and communication skills, capable of acting as a liaison between internal teams, customers, headquarters and local departments.
Language & Tools
: Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications; essential to have Chinese language proficiency (written and spoken) to facilitate communication with headquarters. 
Qualifications
: Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering or related fields is preferred.
Work Experience
: Minimum 3 years of relevant quality management experience in the manufacturing industry, with exposure to QAQC inspection, equipment calibration and supplier quality management being desirable.

Primarily responsible for ensuring that all concrete-related materials, activities, and final products meet the required quality standards, project specifications, and regulatory requirements. Developed concrete mix designs based on customer specifications and requirements.

Coordinating with project managers, site managers, consultants, clients, and third-party inspectors regarding quality matters.
Problem Solving:
 Investigating recurring quality issues and finding the root cause to implement effective solutions and process improvements.
Involvement in CIDB PPS and ISO accreditation, focusing on product compliance (PPS) and management system quality (ISO).

Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field.

Strong technical knowledge of concrete production processes, testing methods, and quality control principles.
Excellent problem-solving, analytical, and decision-making skills.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

Having own transport.
Can be easily contacted.
